data.name: Shivamaya
data.gender_notes: Shivamaya is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Shivamaya is a unisex name derived from the Sanskrit words 'Shiva' and 'Maya', meaning 'Divine Shiva' and 'Illusion' respectively. The name Shivamaya carries the meaning “Divine Shiva” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Shivamaya usually hope their child will grow to embody divine shiva and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Represents the divine aspect of Lord Shiva and the illusionary nature of reality.
data.etymology: Shivamaya belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Divine Shiva.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Shivamaya total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Shivamaya holds deep significance in Hindu culture as Shiva is one of the three major gods in the Hindu pantheon. He is the supreme god of destruction and regeneration, lord of both time and the cosmos. Naming a child Shivamaya would instill in them the traits associated with Lord Shiva, such as detachment, purity of mind, and the ability to end cycles and begin anew. Additionally, using the name Shivamaya would honor and pay homage to the rich cultural heritage and traditions of the Hindu faith.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, the name Shivamaya carries profound meaning. It symbolizes the illusion of reality and the transient nature of all things. Just as Maya (illusion) surrounds Shiva (the Supreme Reality), our day-to-day life is an illusion that deceives us from perceiving the underlying reality. It serves as a constant reminder to reflect upon the eternal truth that lies beyond the material world. Therefore, bearing the name Shivamaya can inspire a deep sense of introspection, contemplation, and spiritual growth in an individual.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Shivamaya signifies the embodiment of Shiva, the divine destroyer and transformer, within one's own consciousness. It symbolizes the pursuit of self-realization through the path of Shiva, leading to inner peace and enlightenment.

vedic_reference.note: This name combines two powerful Sanskrit words: 'Shiva' and 'Maya'. Shiva is the divine consciousness, the supreme reality, the ultimate truth, and the destroyer of evil and ignorance. Maya is the divine power or energy of Lord Shiva that creates, sustains, and dissolves the universe.

historical_references.reference: According to the Shiv Purana, Shivamaya is one of the 108 names of Lord Shiva. The name Shivamaya signifies the one who is in the consciousness of Shiva. Shivamaya is considered to be the embodiment of pure consciousness and self-realization.
historical_references.time_period: Unknown, but the Shiv Purana is believed to have been written between 5th and 16th centuries CE

historical_references.reference: Another reference to Shivamaya comes from the Skanda Purana. In this text, Shivamaya is described as the wife of Lord Shiva during his avataras, particularly during the Rudra and Bhairava forms. She is said to be the source of Shiva's power and strength during these periods.
historical_references.time_period: Unknown, but the Skanda Purana is believed to have been written between 6th and 10th centuries CE

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Shivamaya' holds deep significance in Hinduism, representing the divine essence of Shiva - the God of Destruction and Renewal. In today's world, this name is popularly used on various platforms to symbolize spiritual growth, wellness, and inner peace. On Instagram, #Shivamaya is a popular hashtag for posts related to Hindu spirituality, meditation practices, and inspirational quotes. On YouTube, channels like 'Shivamaya TV' provide guided meditation sessions, spiritual discourses, and insights into Hindu mythology. Lastly, many meditation apps, such as 'Headspace' and 'Calm', include Shivamaya-inspired content or offer guided meditations using this name to help users connect with their inner self and find mental peace.
